Variants.Content: Saath is located in the old land of Sanor on the northern edge of the Dothraki Sea. Politically, it is within the area where the remnants of Saath, grassland tribes and remaining towns intersect. It is a town, a center where surrounding populations, markets, roads and local power converge. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.
Entry Saath Local families also relied on pastures, ruined wells, horse teams, remaining fields and defense khalasas; if any road, well or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Saath They will also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the old lands of Sarnor; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, and real distances must still be measured by wheels, oars, or horse hooves.

Entry Saath If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Half of the traces left by generations of people in Seas are hidden in the workshops, markets, roof tiles, church bells, and streets that have expanded over the generations. The other half is hidden in the memories of the former high kings, the destroyed city, and the gods swallowed up by the sea of ​​grass. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Saath They care about pastures, ruined wells, horse teams, remaining acres of land, and the defense of the khalasa. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection, and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see the coat of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
